---
title: "Primary School Survey 2026"
description: "What households, school staff and boards of management told the Department of Education about primary school ethos."
---

Part of [Religion in Ireland](index.qmd). See also [Schools](schools.qmd) for who runs Ireland's primary schools today.

Over 90% of Irish mainstream primary schools are denominational, yet recent survey data (June 2026) shows substantial and widespread household demand for multi-denominational education. The charts and maps below explore that gap, school by school and county by county, with a particular focus on how the preferences of households differ from those of school staff and boards of management.

The data comes from the Department of Education and Youth's [2025–2026 Primary School Survey](https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-education/campaigns/primary-school-survey/): its [results summary report](../figures/sources/Primary_School_Survey_Results_Summary_Report_June_2026.pdf) (PDF, June 2026; the links on this page go to a copy kept on this site, because the direct link to the PDF on gov.ie returns an error), its [results for all primary schools](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/raw/main/analysis/charts/data/raw/Primary_School_Results_For_All_Primary_Schools.xlsx) and its [School Planning Area results](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/raw/main/analysis/charts/data/raw/Primary_School_Survey_School_Planning_Area_Results.xlsx) (spreadsheets, as published on the survey page; the links are to the copies this site uses). The results for staff and boards of management are not in the spreadsheets, only in the summary report. The code is [on GitHub](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/tree/main/analysis). The figures are interactive, and each one has buttons to download its data as a CSV file, save it as an image, or share it.

These findings were presented at the Department's Annual Education Research Summit on 5 November 2026: [see the slides](#presentation).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## How the numbers are counted

- **National and county shares of households and of staff and boards** (45%, 40.2%, 34.7%, Figures 1, 2, 5 and 6) are the Department's own, from the summary report. They cover **all primary schools, mainstream and special**. They match the School Planning Area results, which also include special schools, and schools whose own results were held back because too few households answered: the planning-area spreadsheet gives 90,177 of 200,365 households (45.0%) preferring a multi-denominational school. Special schools are a small part of these totals: the 119 special schools with a published result account for 2,010 household responses, about 1% of the total.
- **Counts of schools** (Figure 3, Figure 4 and Table 1) come from the results for each school, because only they say which school is which. They cover **mainstream primary schools only** (3,067 in the survey). The 150 special schools are left out: the Department's school lists, which give each school's ethos and location, cover mainstream schools only, and the survey file labels many special schools run by the HSE or disability charities as "Denominational". The shares of pupils and schools that are multi-denominational today (Figure 2) are also for mainstream schools. 180 denominational schools had too few responses for their result to be published.
- **"Most households want a multi-denominational ethos"** has two definitions on this page. *Current households*: more than 50% of the households with children in the school who answered prefer a multi-denominational ethos. This is the result each school received, and it gives **485 schools**. *Current and preschool households*: 50% or more of all households linked to the school, adding households with children not yet in school who named it, prefer a multi-denominational ethos. This gives **573 schools**. 471 schools meet both.
:::

## The first survey of its kind

The Department described the survey as "the largest of its kind ever undertaken in Ireland" (press release, 4 November 2025).

::: {.ethos-cards}
::: {.ethos-card}
### What the Department set out to do

"Assess parental demand for different types of primary school provision": ethos, co-education or single-sex, and English- or Irish-medium.
:::

::: {.ethos-card}
### Who was asked

- Households with children **in** primary school, and with children **not yet enrolled**
- One response per household, validated by Eircode
- Separately, school staff and boards of management
:::
:::

::: {.timeline}
::: {.timeline-step}
**4 Nov 2025**

Survey opens online
:::
::: {.timeline-step}
**16 Dec 2025**

Survey closes: 200,381 valid household and 32,901 staff and board responses
:::
::: {.timeline-step}
**7 Apr 2026**

National household results published
:::
::: {.timeline-step}
**June 2026**

Each school receives its own report. The summary report adds county results for households and for staff and boards
:::
::: {.timeline-step .is-next}
**Oct–Nov 2026**

Boards decide whether to act on their results
:::
:::

Staff and board results are published nationally and by county, but not school by school, for privacy reasons.

## Preference far exceeds current provision

<iframe src="../figures/preference_vs_provision.html" width="100%" height="270" style="border:0" title="Chart: share of households preferring multi-denominational schools, against the share of pupils and schools that are multi-denominational today" loading="lazy"></iframe>

**Figure 2.** The share of households that prefer a multi-denominational school, against the share of pupils and of schools that are multi-denominational today. Sources: households, results summary report, [Table 2a, p. 16](../figures/sources/Primary_School_Survey_Results_Summary_Report_June_2026.pdf#page=16) (all households: 90,189 of 200,381), which the [School Planning Area results](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/raw/main/analysis/charts/data/raw/Primary_School_Survey_School_Planning_Area_Results.xlsx) match (45.0%); pupils and schools, Department of Education, [Data on Individual Schools, mainstream primary 2025/26 (preliminary)](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/raw/main/analysis/charts/data/raw/Data_on_Individual_Schools_Mainstream_2025_26_preliminary.xlsx), as published on [gov.ie](https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-education/collections/data-on-individual-schools/) (see [Schools](schools.qmd)). **Schools covered:** households, all primary schools, mainstream and special, as the Department counted them; pupils and schools today, mainstream primary schools only. Code: [`make_maps.py`](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/blob/main/analysis/charts/make_maps.py).

<iframe src="../figures/map2_current_vs_preference.html" width="100%" height="780" style="border:0" title="Two maps of mainstream denominational schools where most households want a multi-denominational ethos: current households only, and current and preschool households together" loading="lazy"></iframe>

**Figure 3.** Mainstream denominational schools where most households want a multi-denominational ethos (orange), on two definitions side by side. **Left:** households with children currently in the school, where more than 50% prefer a multi-denominational ethos: 485 schools. **Right:** households with children currently in the school together with households with children not yet in school who named it, where 50% or more prefer a multi-denominational ethos: 573 schools. 471 schools are on both maps; 14 are only on the left, and 102 only on the right. Green: the 156 schools that are already multi-denominational. Grey: 180 denominational schools with too few responses for the Department to publish a result. One of the 485, Bunscoil Fachtna (Cork), has no location in the Department's school lists, so it is counted but not drawn. Click the legend to show or hide a group on both maps, and hover over or tap a school for its results. Data: Department of Education and Youth, [Primary School Survey results for all primary schools](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/raw/main/analysis/charts/data/raw/Primary_School_Results_For_All_Primary_Schools.xlsx) (spreadsheet, as published on the [survey page](https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-education/campaigns/primary-school-survey/)); locations and ethos from [Data on Individual Schools, mainstream primary 2024/25](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/raw/main/analysis/charts/data/raw/Data_on_Individual_Schools_Mainstream_2024_25.xlsx) ([gov.ie](https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-education/collections/data-on-individual-schools/)). The CSV lists every mainstream school with its results on both definitions. **Schools covered:** mainstream primary schools only; the 150 special schools are left out. Code: [`make_maps.py`](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/blob/main/analysis/charts/make_maps.py). [Open full screen](../figures/map2_current_vs_preference.html).

## County by county

How many denominational schools have households that want a multi-denominational ethos varies a lot across the country: from almost half of the schools in Wicklow to none in Longford. Use the menu on the map to switch between the two definitions.

<iframe src="../figures/county_multid_map.html" width="100%" height="760" style="border:0" title="Map of Irish counties: share of denominational schools where households want a multi-denominational ethos" loading="lazy"></iframe>

**Figure 4.** Share of mainstream denominational schools with a published result where households want a multi-denominational ethos, by county. Default: more than 50% of households with children in the school. Menu: 50% or more of current and preschool households together. Both views use the same colour scale. **Schools covered:** mainstream primary schools only; the 150 special schools are left out. Data: Department of Education and Youth, [Primary School Survey results for all primary schools](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/raw/main/analysis/charts/data/raw/Primary_School_Results_For_All_Primary_Schools.xlsx) ([survey page](https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-education/campaigns/primary-school-survey/)); ethos from [Data on Individual Schools, mainstream primary 2024/25](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/raw/main/analysis/charts/data/raw/Data_on_Individual_Schools_Mainstream_2024_25.xlsx) ([gov.ie](https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-education/collections/data-on-individual-schools/)). Code: [`make_maps.py`](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/blob/main/analysis/charts/make_maps.py). [Open full screen](../figures/county_multid_map.html).

**Table 1.** Mainstream denominational schools in each county: how many there are, how many are Catholic and how many are Church of Ireland or another faith (including inter-denominational schools), how many have a published survey result, and how many of those have households wanting a multi-denominational ethos on each definition. Shares are of the schools with a published result. Click a column heading to sort. The CSV also splits each count into Catholic and other faiths. **Schools covered:** mainstream primary schools only; the 150 special schools are left out. Data: as Figure 4.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## How the staff and board of management survey was run

The school staff and board of management survey was open to primary school staff and members of boards of management nationally. The target population was 84,285 staff and board members. A total of 32,999 responses were submitted, and 32,901 valid responses were kept after validation. That is a validated response rate of 39.0% of the eligible population. (Source: results summary report, [section 4.1, p. 25](../figures/sources/Primary_School_Survey_Results_Summary_Report_June_2026.pdf#page=25).)
:::

## There is a mismatch between the schools households want for their children and the schools available to them

<iframe src="../figures/vis2_intend_vs_preference.html" width="100%" height="420" style="border:0" title="Chart: ethos preference among households with a child not yet in school, by intended school type" loading="lazy"></iframe>

**Figure 6.** Stated ethos preference among households with a child not yet in school (n = 56,227), grouped by the type of school they intend to use. Each bar is 100% of the households intending that school type, split by whether they prefer a multi-denominational (green) or denominational (grey) ethos. This isolates demand for change: households intending a denominational school but preferring a multi-denominational one represent unmet demand, while households intending and preferring the same type represent confirmed preference. Percentages are recomputed from raw counts reported in the source, and the base (56,227) can't be independently checked against the published survey spreadsheet. Source: Department of Education and Youth, Primary School Survey results summary report (June 2026), [section 3.1.2, p. 14](../figures/sources/Primary_School_Survey_Results_Summary_Report_June_2026.pdf#page=14). **Schools covered:** all primary schools, mainstream and special, as the Department counted them. Code: [`make_charts.py`](https://github.com/fianaise/fianaise.ie/blob/main/analysis/charts/make_charts.py).
